newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans say 300 refugees killed by Tutsi rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans say 300 refugees killed by Tutsi rebels.

text.p: Tutsi rebels massacred more than 300 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees at a camp 40 kilometres (25 miles) southwest of the regional capital Bukavu, local Zaireans said on Monday.

Residents of nearby Kakinda village and a survivor said that on November 17 up to 40 rebels gathered 310 refugees at Chimanga camp saying they would be repatriated, and then set off a mortar or a grenade and killed survivors with automatic rifles.

Residents, who said they were ordered silent on the massacre by rebels, showed Reuters journalists a series of graves where they had buried bodies, several bodies and a female survivor injured and hiding in a nearby field.
Blood stained clothes, children's and women's slippers were left on the camp square where the shooting took place.
Up to 30,000 Hutu refugees lived at Chimanga Camp, but most fled last month after fighting broke out between ethnic Tutsi rebels who now control much of Eastern Zaire and the Zairean army.

Residents, who said they feared revenge from the rebels, showed journalists the decomposing bodies of a women and three children lying on the rubble of a clay hut. They said they saw the woman wounded on Sunday and said rebels returned the next day and shot her dead.
Journalists found a young female refugee from Rwanda who survived the massacre and was hiding in a nearby corn field after being injured in the leg and arm.
More than one million mainly-Rwandan refugees fled camps around Goma, Bukavu and Uvira last month after the fighting started between rebels and the Zairean army.

The Rwandan refugees first fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals from the victorious Rwandan Patriotic Front after a genocide of up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus organised by Hutu extremists in the former government.
Around 500,000 Rwandan Hutus returned to Rwanda from camps around Goma between November 15 and 19 after being dislodged from the camps by Tutsi rebels.
